This appendix describes how the Investigators experiment application is implemented, for readers who need to understand or audit the system. It is regenerated for every build; its tables are read from the code they describe. It intentionally omits recruitment-platform integration, participant identifiers and payment details.

## 1. Components

- **API** (`backend/app`, FastAPI + SQLAlchemy Core on PostgreSQL): the participant and admin HTTP surfaces. Every participant mutation is a *command* executed in one transaction that first locks the session row (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, `app.db.tx.execute_command`), so commands for one session apply strictly in order.
- **Worker** (`app.workers.main`): claims scheduled jobs. A dispatch thread runs timing jobs (warnings, deadlines, deliveries, check-ins); a separate generation thread runs model-backed `generate` jobs so a slow model call never delays a due timing job.
- **Local model** (Ollama, loopback only): grounded generation for teammate social replies and the AI assistant, pinned by model digest; every output passes a deterministic validator and falls back to pinned scripted text on any failure.
- **UI** (`frontend`, React + Vite, static nginx image): a server-driven stage router. The simultaneous workbench mounts case file, team chat and AI assistant at once; all state transitions arrive through the event feed and session snapshot.

## 2. Profiles, binding and policy

A session pins one published *manifest* (profile) and its content artifacts by SHA-256 (`content/published/manifests.json` is add-only). Binding resolves the manifest to an executable `ResolvedPolicy`; its canonical hash (`behavior_policy_hash`) is part of each session's compatibility key. The two arms of a profile may differ only under `manipulation.arm.*` (checked on every build).

New live batch groups may pin an optional, versioned `enrollment_policy`: an allowed platform, exact member/arm cells, and a valid-completer target per cell. Consenting participants receive a random tie-break among the least-occupied eligible cells. Retained-data completions and active allocated sessions hold capacity; terminal dropouts release capacity without changing their old allocation. The allocator and completion handler serialize on the group row, after the participant's own session lock. The group closes when every target is reached. Uncapped historical groups retain their existing permuted-block behavior. A separate test-only policy requires TEST_ IDs, records zero-cent ineligible entitlements, and excludes these sessions from the compensation queue.

The **interaction mode** feature flag (FR-1) is arm-invariant. `structured_and_nl` offers per-crate request controls plus free text; `nl_only` never opens `structured_seeking` and refuses crate-only assistant asks (`structured_request_disabled`) — a typed teammate ask naming a crate instead routes each responder into per-seat structured retrieval, delivering that seat's own latest record card (O-1). ## 4. Commands and transactions

Each command carries a client UUID and the expected session revision. The handler runs inside one transaction that appends events, updates projections, schedules jobs and writes a *receipt*; replaying the same UUID returns the stored receipt, and a stale revision is refused (`stale_revision`) so the client resyncs and retries under a new UUID. Bodies are bounded (64 KiB) and validated before any state is touched. Command kinds and the stages that accept them:

## 5. Scheduler and timing

Time-dependent behavior is a durable `scheduled_job` row with a logical key, a clock basis (`active` task time, which pauses during check-ins, or `wall`) and a lease. Workers claim due jobs with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, execute them inside the session transaction (`finish_job`), and expired leases are reclaimed; retries reuse the job's pinned inputs so outcomes never re-roll. Job kinds:

`checkin`, `connecting`, `task_open`, `solo_review_end`, `checkin`, `checkin_reveal`, `checkin_inactivity`, `deadline`, `warning`, `greeting_prompt`, `scripted_request`, `pressure_remark`, `generate`, `qa_answer`, `chat_judge`, `deliver`

## 6. Generation pipeline

0. Free-text team messages route first: `engines.addressed_seats` picks the responder set (addressed seat, or both seats for broadcast/undirected text — O-2). Automation probes get a pinned verbatim disclosure line without a model call (O-3), answered by the seat the probe is about (`probed_seats` — a third-person "is pm a bot?" discloses from PM, relational "is your teammate a bot?" resolves to the other seat, coordinated "are you and pm bots?" hits both — O-11/BA-65/BA-66); a probe can never be refused by the ordinary pending-request cap or the operational rate limit and is always logged as an `automation_probe` event — disclosure *scheduling* instead gets its own bounded per-seat budget of unfinished (pending or claimed) probe lines (BA-75). Probe-adjacent non-fires flag `probe_near_miss` on `message_accepted` for review (O-12/BA-67). In `nl_only` a typed intel ask routes each responder into per-seat record delivery (crate references accept digits, number words, ordinals and `#N`; a bare crate-numbered follow-up counts as the ask; a leading seat address like "jt, crate 3" scopes it to that seat; multi-clause messages resolve the crate in the *asking* clause — "i have crate 3. what about crate 4?" asks about 4 — BA-52/O-12/BA-62/BA-64), while in structured modes the same ask gets the deterministic picker-redirect line (BA-53/BA-63); first-person statements ("i have crate 3") are not asks (BA-64); assignment/no-holdings asks get grounded verbatim lines — none of these schedule a `generate` job.
1. On accept, the command pins a `knowledge_snapshot` (record ids + SHA-256 for the assistant; open request episodes for teammates) and schedules a `generate` job.
2. The generation thread builds a grounded prompt from the snapshot only (`app.services.prompts`): untrusted text is quoted inside `<<< >>>` blocks with delimiters escaped; teammate prompts carry the seat's style block, a bounded RECENT CHAT window of the latest multi-actor team turns — including participant share events, which never write a message row (BA-68) — with card deliveries and shares shown as `[shared a record card on crate N]` placeholders (O-14), an OPEN ASKS block scoped to asks the responding seat is part of (BA-69), and its own earlier team lines as no-repeat context (cards as placeholders there too) — record bodies never reach a social prompt (AID-55).
3. The provider call has one end-to-end deadline (identity check, queue, HTTP, bounded body read). Each call carries a per-job `derived_seed(session_id, job_id)` forwarded as the OpenAI `seed`, and `model_call.parameters` records the seed plus the load the call competed with (`concurrent_sessions`, `claimed_generate`, `queued_generate`, `provider_inflight_local` — O-18/O-20; `claimed_generate` counts scheduler-claimed jobs across workers (DB-level), `provider_inflight_local` the adapter's process-local in-flight counter — BA-70). Failed calls persist the effective request params, the seed, a `dispatched` marker distinguishing pre-wire from on-wire failures (connection refusals and DNS failures count as never-dispatched), and measured latency (BA-71).
4. Inside the session lock the output is validated; the assistant's location claims are also checked against the pinned records. A rejected, empty, failed or late output is recorded on `model_call` and replaced by deterministic fallback text (fallback lines also skip anything already sent; a pool that exhausts wraps to its start, recorded via `draw_ordinal`/`pool_wrapped` on `voice_line_committed` and `repeated_line` on `message_delivered` — O-17).
5. A `deliver` job commits the message at its scheduled active time.

Validator `teammate_output_v8` violation classes: `banned_token_reuse`, `condition_leak`, `disrespect`, `evaluation`, `hideout_leak`, `human_claim`, `interface_leak`, `length_overrun`, `near_repeat`, `prompt_reveal`, `record_ref_leak`, `repeat_message`, `stall_excuse`, `task_advice`, `unverified_source`, `urgency`, `voice_format`. Repeat rule (BA-60): generated text and pool-drawn fallback lines of at least 3 words may never be sent twice by teammates in a session (comparison ignores case, spacing, apostrophes and hyphens — BA-57). The `near_repeat` class (v7, 2026-10-04 lab walkthrough) also rejects a line of at least 6 distinct words sharing ≥75% distinct-word Dice overlap with a delivered line — convergent cross-seat near-paraphrases read as one scripted reply. If a repeat or near-paraphrase is detected at delivery, an unused pool line (itself skipping exact and near repeats) is substituted and the event is flagged `repeat_substituted` + `repeat_substituted_reason` ("exact"/"near"); a repeat that still ships flags `repeated_line`/`near_repeat_line` on `message_delivered` (O-17). Pinned *verbatim* lines — the automation disclosure, grounded assignment/no-holdings statements and the picker redirect — are exempt by design: their truth and consistency outrank variety.

Teammate voices (prompt builder style blocks):

- **JT** — Your own style as JT: brief and low key. Mostly lower case, a dry sense of humor, short clipped phrases, words like yeah, np, ok, sure.
- **PM** — Your own style as PM: friendly and a bit more talkative than JT. Normal capitalization, full short sentences, words like sounds good, thanks for that, happy to.

### 6.1 Task-shape conditions (crate distribution experiment)

The `task` block of a manifest can pin a non-legacy world shape (`overlap_v1` generator): `crate_overlap` (`none` = 12 crates with disjoint four-crate seat assignments, `some` = 8 crates with all three pairwise assignment intersections held to 1–2 crates, `full` = 4 crates shared by every seat) and `participant_intel_budget` (20 — the only supported thin-file value). The administered shape persists in `world_snapshot.content.world_params` (`n_crates`, `n_assigned`, `crate_overlap`, `participant_intel_budget`, `covered_unassigned`) and every consumer — workbench descriptors, replay, exports, the power workflow — resolves it snapshot-first, never from deployment flags.

**Comparability note (audit G04):** the conditions hold the experimental constants fixed — four assigned crates per participant, two own-file and two team-dependent solvability roles, six hideouts, and the latest-record truth rule. What varies is the surrounding world: total crate count (4/8/12), participant file density (full world ≈47–49 records vs the 20-record thin file), the count of unassigned crates the participant's file covers (all unassigned crates under legacy/`some`, a limited asked-plus-fill set under `none`, none under `full`), and which crates scripted teammate asks can target (full-overlap seats can only ask about the shared four). `crate_overlap` and `intel_budget` are therefore *experimental factors*, not nuisance covariates: they must appear as stratification or factor terms in any approved pooled analysis, and the power workflow refuses mixed-cell inputs absent an explicit condition spec. Accuracy denominators are unchanged (four assigned crates), but seeking opportunities, file coverage measures and the request surface differ by design across levels.

## 7. Participant projection

Participants only ever receive allowlisted event types and payload keys (`app.services.projection.PARTICIPANT_EVENTS`); arm labels, truth, teammate holdings and implementation vocabulary never leave the server, and the built bundle is scanned for leaked vocabulary on every gate. Allowlisted event types:

`teammate_presented`, `task_clock_started`, `task_deadline`, `warning_committed`, `answers_frozen`, `resumed`, `technical_stop`, `message_delivered`, `message_accepted`, `greeting_prompt`, `teammate_requested`, `assistant_requested`, `record_shared`, `record_added_to_file`, `checkin_open`, `checkin_response`, `checkin_reveal`, `qa_asked`, `qa_answered`, `stage_proceeded`, `answer_updated`, `confidence_recorded`, `item_recorded`, `instrument_complete`, `consent_recorded`, `training_started`, `training_step`, `debrief_acknowledged`, `data_use_recorded`, `session_completed`, `writer_takeover`

## 8. Persistence

All tables live in the `app` schema; migrations are Alembic, and the API refuses readiness when the database head differs from the build's. Export boundaries (BA-60): a research export contains committed rows from session-owned `app` tables only — it omits `participant_display` (participant display initials are identity-adjacent and never leave), all `identity.*` tables (platform linkage), and payment-domain tables (entitlement, receipt, result). Platform linkage plus payment state appears only in the restricted compensation product (`export_payment_linkage` / `app.export.restricted`), which must run as the `investigators_compensation` role and returns nothing else session-owned. Drift guards in `app.export.study` fail the export if a restricted or display table ever becomes passthrough.

## 9. Provenance and builds

There is no Git tree: a build is identified by the SHA-256 over `backend/`, `frontend/`, `content/` and `docker-compose.yml` (`scripts/source_bundle.py`). Images are stamped with it and report it on API `/version` and UI `version.json`; pinned inputs are verified against `docs/baseline/SOURCE_CHECKSUMS.sha256`. Each build also regenerates this appendix and the click-through mock (`docs/clickthrough/investigators_clickthrough.html`).
